key_insight: Vis-Lens generates natural-looking images preferred by neural targets by directly modifying activation-regularized latent codes, without per-image iterative optimization.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports neural-network interpretability by generating realistic images that reveal the visual patterns favored by selected units.
method: Structure a visual representation landscape using an activation-based prior.
Integrate a variational autoencoder and a diffusion model for image generation.
Modify activation-regularized latent codes to target brain regions or artificial neural units.
evidence_signal: Evaluations on artificial neural networks and human visual cortex using fMRI data report improved activation modulation and image realism over a recent state-of-the-art method.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative gains or computational costs, leaving the practical size of the improvement unclear.
paper_title: Structured Visual Landscape: Generating Preferred Representations in Biological and Artificial Neural Networks
